summary: Minecraft/Discord/browser credential stealer and Minecraft mods dropper disguised as a TOTP library
details: The package advertises itself as a zero-dependency TOTP/HOTP 2FA helper, but lib/core.js is a credential-harvesting and post-exploitation payload. On first API call, gated by USERPROFILE+Documents and by an _env() check that bails out under CI/CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION/JEST_WORKER_ID/audit/pack contexts, it (1) reads Minecraft account stores for Vanilla, Lunar, Essential, CurseForge, and Modrinth launchers, plus the DPAPI-protected launcher_msa_credentials_microsoft_store.bin, uses login.live.com and Xbox Live/XSTS OAuth to exchange MSA refresh tokens for fresh Minecraft SSIDs, and multipart-uploads each account (JWT, MSA refresh token, rotated refresh token, UUID) to a hardcoded Discord webhook; (2) enumerates Discord, Discord Canary/PTB/Development, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Opera GX Local Storage leveldb directories, extracts plain and dQw4w9WgXcQ:-prefixed Discord tokens, spawns PowerShell ProtectedData.Unprotect to recover each Chromium DPAPI master key, AES-256-GCM decrypts the tokens, validates them against discord.com/api/v9/users/@me, and posts valid tokens to the same webhook; and (3) downloads a jar from github.com/ghysghqgHUJ/.jar/releases/download/v1.0.0/fabric-api-boost-1.0.0.jar and writes it as fabric-api-boost-1.0.0.jar into every discovered Minecraft mods folder (.minecraft/mods, ModrinthApp profiles,.lunarclient offline), so the next Minecraft launch loads attacker-controlled Java bytecode. Sensitive strings (the Discord webhook, discord.com host, powershell.exe, ProtectedData, child_process, Xbox Live auth headers, dropper jar URL) are XOR-0x3F encoded byte arrays reconstructed at runtime via Buffer.from(a.map(b => b ^ 0x3F)).toString().

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
